events.title: REST architectural style defined
events.summary: Roy Fielding's 2000 doctoral dissertation defined Representational State Transfer (REST) — an architectural style for scalable network APIs using HTTP resources and hypermedia.
events.about: REST is not a library — it is a design approach: expose resources as URLs, use HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), keep servers stateless, and cache responses. Most 'REST APIs' today are HTTP+JSON without hypermedia, but the dissertation still names the constraints teams aim for. Fielding co-authored HTTP/1.1 while writing it.

narrative.whyChosen: REST gave a vocabulary for why the web's architecture scales — and influenced every public HTTP API since.
narrative.whyImportant: It separated resource design from RPC-style endpoints and became the default mental model for web services.
narrative.problemSolved: Ad-hoc HTTP APIs lacked shared constraints; developers needed principles for cacheable, layered, scalable systems.

events.title: Fabrice Bellard creates FFmpeg
events.summary: Fabrice Bellard started FFmpeg in 2000 — the multimedia toolkit behind YouTube transcoding, VLC, and countless video pipelines.
events.about: FFmpeg's libavcodec/libavformat power video on the web — every streaming service transcodes with it or derivatives. Bellard also created QEMU and co-authored AV1-related research.

narrative.whyChosen: FFmpeg is the invisible engine behind web video encoding.
narrative.whyImportant: It standardized open multimedia processing across platforms.
narrative.problemSolved: Proprietary codecs and tools made video processing expensive and fragmented.

events.title: JetBrains founded
events.summary: JetBrains was founded in 2000 in Prague — starting as IntelliJ s.r.o. before shipping IntelliJ IDEA and growing into a family of language-specific IDEs.
events.about: JetBrains built the IDE stack many developers live in: IntelliJ IDEA for Java, then RubyMine, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, and the Kotlin language itself. Its IntelliJ Platform also powers Android Studio and Google's language tooling partnerships.

narrative.whyChosen: JetBrains became the dominant independent IDE vendor outside Microsoft and Apple.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved deep static analysis and refactoring could be a sustainable product business.
narrative.problemSolved: Java and polyglot teams needed smarter tooling than free Eclipse plugins could deliver.
